narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and your credit history. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have accounts in this state, while the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This negative status strongly signaled higher risk to the model.

The 42-month duration you requested was the second most important factor and also increased your risk score. Approved loans average only 19 months, so your longer term stood out as substantially above the norm.

Your credit history marked as “critical or other credits” worked in the opposite direction. This actually pulled the prediction slightly toward approval. However, its positive influence was not strong enough to overcome the negative effects of your account status and loan length.

Given these results, you should first bring your checking account balance into positive territory and consider applying for a shorter-term loan. Improving your overall credit profile over the next few months would also help your chances on a future application.
